newsitem.title: USA: Calif. utility infrastructure seen fully developed.
newsitem.headline: Calif. utility infrastructure seen fully developed.

text.p: Municipal and investor-owned utilities in the western U.S. will not need to finance major new infrastructure projects in the near-term, a Southern California Edison official said on Friday.
Vikram Budhraja, a Southern California Edison senior vice president, told a conference here that the western U.S. already has more transmission and generation than it needs.

"I think it is fair to say that our infrastructure for both transmission and generation is fully developed," Budhraja said. "In the case of generation, we have excess capacity and I don't see the need for major new projects in the near future."
Budhraja spoke on a utility deregulation panel at the Bond Buyer California public finance conference in Marina Del Rey.
The commissioner of the California Public Utilities Commission, Daniel Fessler, who also spoke on the panel, said deregulation was an "economic necessity" in the state.

"California cannot then and cannot now, as we begin to recover (from the recession), afford to pay more for the fundamentals of maintaining a commercial, industrial and agricultural economy," Fessler said.
